messages:
marie: Quick sync 1: we shipped GA yesterday, there's a small follow-up plan on my table. Two urgent bugs + one UX tweak. Question: single micropatch or stagger across two releases?
alex: What's the risk surface if we bundle everything?
sam: Crash on multi-chunk prompts (seen in support tickets) and a backend token accounting miscount under heavy syncs. Crash is reproducible; accounting causes billing noise. Both customer-visible.
marie: UX tweak is an inline helper text during onboarding (low-risk). My leaning: stagger to minimize rollback impact.
luis: Stagger helps isolate the crash fix. If the crash fix causes performance regression we can rollback without touching the accounting change. Also gives us time to monitor invoicing signals.
tina: We should make the enhancement release-first only if crash will take >36h. It reduces support load and buys time.
sam: I can prioritize crash patch and have a canary within 18h. Need freeze on non-critical merges to api and runtime for ~12h.
alex: If canary is green, follow with accounting fix + microcopy in second micro-release next day. Deploy windows: do both during low-traffic slot 02:00 PT.
marie: Acceptance criteria for crash patch: repro test added, <=1% error rate for long-prompt SLA, smoke job covering 5 large customers. For accounting: no double-counting in synthetic load. For ux: copy reviewed by tina.
luis: Add observability: a short-lived histogram for token delta per sync and a dashboard tag patch/micro-4281234567. Ops will watch for 12h post-deploy.
ops-bot: Added temporary alert: accounting-delta > 0.5% -> paging oncall.
deploy-bot: Suggested pipeline: canary/4281234567-crash -> wait 4h -> promote/4281234567-1. If green, schedule promote/4281234567-2 (accounting+ux) 24h later. Manual gates: marie + alex signoff.
sam: I'll open PRs now and include a tiny CI job: run-long-prompt.sh with 10 customer seeds. Pasting snippet:
```
./run-long-prompt.sh --seeds 10 --repeat 3
```
marie: Good. Tagging owners: sam (crash fix), alex (accounting), tina (ux copy + QA). I'll create backlog items: patch:micro/crash-4281234567, patch:micro/accounting-4281234567, patch:micro/ux-4281234567.
alex: One more: add a rollback policy in the release notes: full rollback if error rate >2% or lat p99 increases >200ms over baseline.
maria: noted (typo: marie meant).
luis: We'll coordinate customer comms only if any regressions hit >50 users. Otherwise internal incident notes.
marie: Quick sync 11:30 to confirm freeze and signoffs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
